description: Point-in-time analyst 12-month price targets per ticker. Targets are the Bloomberg consensus mean ("12M Tgt Px") paired with the contemporaneous Bloomberg price, so the implied upside is source-consistent and independent of the Yahoo price series the backtest trades on. Dates are AS-OF: a lookup at time t must take the newest row with date <= t. Every ticker carries the universe `tier` it entered through ('core' = UNIVERSE_JK, 'lq45' = LQ45 names the archive was missing, 'broad' = wider IHSG names) — see data/universe.js. Read via data/analyst-views.js — do not hand-edit.

bloomberg.precedence: a ticker belongs to the FIRST file listed that carries it; later blocks for the same name are skipped, not merged

capture.role: dated dispersion + analyst coverage (Omega); contributes no targets

dividends.role: DATED trailing-12-month yield — the y in Q = upside + y

snapshot.role: static per-ticker dividend yield / dispersion / analyst-count fallback

supplements.role: per-ticker corrections for truncated vendor blocks; win on a shared date

notes: Dividend yield in Q = (target - price)/price + y is DATED: a trailing-12-month sum of per-ex-date yield fractions from dividends.json, look-ahead-free (an ex-date counts only once it has passed). Each dividend is measured against the price prevailing when it was paid, so y is the yield actually earned rather than old payments rescaled by a newer price.

APPROXIMATION — names the dividend record does not reach still fall back to the STATIC snapshot yield (one present-day number at every historical step), and to 0 when the snapshot lacks them too. viewAsOf reports which was used via `dividendSource`.
APPROXIMATION — analyst count and target dispersion are static before the first weekly capture (2026-06-19). They drive Black-Litterman Omega only; the target spine itself is fully dated.
Bloomberg rows are Wednesdays; the backtest rebalances on the weekly (Friday) bar, so the as-of lookup picks up a view 2 days old at most on a fresh week. No look-ahead.

The archive is WIDER than the optimizer/forward-test universe. tier=core is the 25 names UNIVERSE_JK trades; tier=lq45 and tier=broad exist so a backtest or sweep can opt into a larger opportunity set. Adding a name here does NOT add it to any fetch script.
Coverage is NOT uniform — see coverage.perTicker. Names with late starts or long gaps fall back to the trailing sample mean at steps the archive cannot cover (see analyst-views.js staleness).
